x_intro_gain: A newborn gains $4.52$ percent of lifetime consumption. About $34$ percent of that gain comes in childhood, from a parent who spends more on the child's consumption and housing and less on drugs, and is less likely to remain unemployed longer because of a SUD, further improving childhood consumption. About $17$ percent comes from the higher earnings of a child whose parent was free of the disorder. The remaining $47$ percent comes from a better economy to live in as an adult: whatever its productivity, an eligible household that stays clean is $42$ percent more likely to get a voucher, paid for by the users the screen excludes and by the higher taxes paid by working-age households that no longer carry the earnings penalty or remain unemployed longer because of a SUD. The other $66$ percent comes in adult life, from two sources. The first, $17$ percent of the whole gain, is the better productivity node a child draws, mostly because its own parent does not carry the disorder.
